formula: log(cost) ~ log(output) + log(pf) + lf + (1 | airline)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: a panel of US airlines over 1970 to 1984 (year coded from 1), total cost, output, fuel price and load factor, referenced to Greene (2003, Table F7.1); the page gives no model. Greene's airline cost function regresses log cost on log output, log fuel price and load factor with airline and year effects (recalled from the cited book, not read; not verified that a random-effects fit is among them), so the panel unit airline is rendered as a random intercept by the panel ruling. year is the time index, left out.

formula: ui ~ rr + I(rr^2) + age + I(age^2) + tenure + joblost + head + married + dkids + dykids + smsa + nwhite + yrdispl + school12 + sex + statemb + stateur + (1 | state)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: displaced blue-collar workers 1982-1991 (McCall 1995) with their state of residence code, the state unemployment rate and the state maximum benefit, referenced to Verbeek (2004, ch. 7). Verbeek's illustration of benefit recipiency fits linear probability, logit and probit models of ui (applied for and received UI benefits) on the replacement rate and its square, age and its square, tenure, the reason the job was lost (slack work, position abolished, seasonal job ended), household head, married, children, young children, SMSA, non-white, year of displacement, more than 12 years of school, male, the state maximum benefit and the state unemployment rate (recalled from the cited book, not read), treating workers as independent. state repeats across workers and carries the state-level covariates, rendered as (1 | state) by the repeating-cluster ruling at low. joblost enters as its factor, other the base. bluecol is constant.

formula: wfood ~ log(totexp) + log(pfood) + log(phouse) + log(pmisc) + (1 | income:size)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: Italian budget shares of food, housing and fuels and miscellaneous goods 1973-1992 (Bollino, Perali and Rossi 2000) with their prices, total expenditure, income, household size and a cell weight pct; the page gives no model. The rows are cells of income class and household size per year, and the cell recurs over the years, a pseudo-panel the page does not name; rendered as (1 | income:size) at low, each share as a linear equation in log total expenditure and log prices. The cited paper estimates a demand system with linear household technologies over the three shares (from its title, not read). The source weights each cell by pct, which the formula leaves out. Rows 2 and 3 are whouse and wmisc. year is the time index, left out.

formula: whouse ~ log(totexp) + log(pfood) + log(phouse) + log(pmisc) + (1 | income:size)
notes: RULE GAP: The housing and fuels share equation of the demand system of row 1, with its grouping and covariates; the source weights each cell by pct, which the formula leaves out.

formula: wmisc ~ log(totexp) + log(pfood) + log(phouse) + log(pmisc) + (1 | income:size)
notes: RULE GAP: The miscellaneous share equation of the demand system of row 1, with its grouping and covariates; the source weights each cell by pct, which the formula leaves out.

formula: testscr ~ str + elpct + mealpct + calwpct + (1 | county)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: California school districts in 1998-1999 with their county; testscr is the mean of readscr and mathscr (alternate responses, ignored), referenced to Stock and Watson (2003, ch. 4-7). The book regresses testscr on the student-teacher ratio, adding the percent of English learners, the percent eligible for reduced-price lunch and the percent qualifying for CalWORKs (recalled from the cited book, not read), treating districts as independent. county repeats across districts, rendered as (1 | county) by the repeating-cluster ruling at low. distcod and district identify the row.

formula: choice ~ brand intercept + disp.<brand> + feat.<brand> + price.<brand> (conditional logit over heinz41, heinz32, heinz28 and hunts32, one coefficient per attribute) + household-varying brand intercepts and attribute coefficients over id (random-coefficients logit)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: repeated catsup purchases of households (id) with each brand's display, feature advertisement and price; the page gives no model. Its source, Jain, Vilcassim and Chintagunta (1994, JBES 12, 317-328), fits by its abstract (IDEAS/RePEc) a random-coefficients logit to household panel data, brand preferences and responses to marketing variables varying across households, the heterogeneity distribution approximated by a discrete distribution. Rendered as a categorical response with household random effects over id; the discrete heterogeneity and the alternative-specific attributes have no lme4 form. family blank: categorical responses are outside the contract's family rule.

formula: log(sales) ~ log(price / cpi) + log(ndi / cpi) + log(pimin / cpi) + (1 | state)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: cigarette sales in packs per capita of US states 1963-1992 with price, CPI, per capita disposable income and the minimum price in adjoining states (Baltagi and Levin 1992; Baltagi, Griffin and Xiong 2000), referenced to Baltagi (2003); the page gives no model. The cited papers estimate a dynamic demand, log sales on lagged log sales, log real price, log real disposable income and log real minimum price in adjoining states, by pooled, within, IV and GMM estimators (recalled, not read; not verified that any is a random-effects fit). The lag is no column and is left out, a dynamic panel rendered static; the panel unit state is a random intercept by the panel ruling. pop and pop16 are unused.

formula: log(packpc) ~ log(avgprs / cpi) + log(income / (pop * cpi)) + (1 | state)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: packs per capita of US states 1985-1995 with CPI, population, state personal income, taxes and the average price including sales taxes, referenced to Stock and Watson (2003, ch. 10). The book's instrumental-variables chapter regresses log packs on log real price, instrumented by the general sales tax (taxs - tax) and the cigarette-specific tax, with log real per capita income, on the 1995 cross-section and on the 1985-1995 differences (recalled, not read); no mixed model. The panel unit state is rendered as a random intercept by the panel ruling; the instruments tax and taxs are left out of the formula.

formula: choice ~ brand intercept + disp.<brand> + feat.<brand> + price.<brand> (conditional logit over sunshine, kleebler, nabisco and private, one coefficient per attribute) + household-varying brand intercepts and attribute coefficients over id (random-coefficients logit)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: repeated cracker purchases of households (id) with each brand's display, feature advertisement and price; the page gives no model. Its sources are Jain, Vilcassim and Chintagunta (1994, JBES 12, 317-328), whose abstract (IDEAS/RePEc) fits a random-coefficients logit to household panel data, brand preferences and responses to marketing variables varying across households with a discrete heterogeneity distribution, and Paap and Franses (2000), a dynamic multinomial probit. Rendered as a categorical response with household random effects over id; the discrete heterogeneity and the alternative-specific attributes have no lme4 form. family blank: categorical responses are outside the contract's family rule.

formula: log(crmrte) ~ log(prbarr) + log(polpc) + log(prbconv) + log(prbpris) + log(avgsen) + log(density) + log(wcon) + log(wtuc) + log(wtrd) + log(wfir) + log(wser) + log(wmfg) + log(wfed) + log(wsta) + log(wloc) + log(pctymle) + log(pctmin) + region + smsa + factor(year) + (1 | county)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: North Carolina counties 1981-1987 (Cornwell and Trumbull 1994; Baltagi 2006), referenced to Baltagi (2003) and linking plm's Crime, the same panel with the logarithms precomputed. plm's vignette (A_plmPackage.Rmd, Instrumental variable estimators, in the pinned plm 2.6-7) fits plm(lcrmrte ~ lprbarr + lpolpc + lprbconv + lprbpris + lavgsen + ldensity + lwcon + lwtuc + lwtrd + lwfir + lwser + lwmfg + lwfed + lwsta + lwloc + lpctymle + lpctmin + region + smsa + factor(year) | . - lprbarr - lpolpc + ltaxpc + lmix, data = Crime, model = "random"), the random-effects 2SLS of Baltagi (2005, p. 120, table 7.3), written here on this table's raw columns. The instruments taxpc and mix for prbarr and polpc are left out, so the formula is the random-effects model without instrumenting; medium for that departure.

formula: mrall ~ beertax + mlda + jaild + comserd + vmiles + unrate + log(perinc) + factor(year) + (1 | state)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: traffic fatality rate (deaths per 10000) of US states 1982-1988 (Ruhm) with the beer tax, minimum legal drinking age, mandatory jail and community service, miles per driver, unemployment rate and per capita income, referenced to Stock and Watson (2003, ch. 8). The book's panel chapter regresses the fatality rate on the beer tax with state, then state and time fixed effects, adding the drinking-age, punishment and economic controls with log real income (recalled, not read); only fixed-effects fits, so the panel unit state is rendered as a random intercept by the panel ruling and the time effects stay as factor(year). The book codes the drinking age as dummies; mlda enters as the age.

formula: lgaspcar ~ lincomep + lrpmg + lcarpcap + (1 | country)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: OECD countries 1960-1978 (Baltagi and Griffin 1983), log gasoline consumption per car, log real income per capita, log real gasoline price and log cars per capita, referenced to Baltagi (2003). Baltagi's one-way error component chapter carries section 2.6.2, Example 2: Gasoline Demand (tables of contents of the 3rd and 6th editions, found by search), which reports OLS, between, within and the random-effects estimators (WALHUS, AMEMIYA, SWAR, IMLE) of this equation; the regressors are recalled, the table not read. year is the time index.

formula: inv ~ value + capital + (1 | firm)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: gross investment, firm value and capital stock of US firms 1935-1954, referenced to Greene (2003, Table F13.1) and Baltagi (2003). plm's vignette B_plmFunction.Rmd (pinned plm 2.6-7, whose Grunfeld Rd compares its table to Baltagi's as the same data set) reproduces Baltagi's table 2.1 one-way error component estimates: ols <- plm(inv ~ value + capital, Grunfeld, model = "pooling"), then update(ols, model = "random", random.method = "walhus") with amemiya and swar; A_plmPackage.Rmd fits the ML version lme(inv ~ value + capital, data = Grunfeld, random = ~1 | firm). year is the time index.

formula: Individuals.Affected ~ Covered.Entity.Type + (1 | State)
notes: RESPONSE INFERRED: Read the Ecdat page: breach reports to the US Department of Health and Human Services of 500 or more compromised records, downloaded 2015-02-26, each with the covered entity, its type, the state where the breach occurred, the records compromised, the breach types and the locations of the information; the examples compute mean(Individuals.Affected) and tabulate breach types and locations, no model. Individuals.Affected (500 or more by law) taken as the response, breaches nested in State, an area factor with many levels, at low. Type.of.Breach and Location.of.Breached.Information combine several categories each and stay as columns outside the formula. Business.Associate.Present is derived from Covered.Entity.Type; Name.of.Covered.Entity and Web.Description are names and narrative text.

formula: mv ~ crim + zn + indus + chas + nox + rm + age + dis + rad + tax + ptratio + blacks + lstat + (1 | townid)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: Boston census tracts (Harrison and Rubinfeld 1978) with their town identifier, referenced to Baltagi (2003); the columns carry Harrison and Rubinfeld's transforms (mv and lstat in logs, rm and nox squared, as the first rows show). plm's vignette A_plmPackage.Rmd (section Unbalanced panels, pinned plm 2.6-7) fits Hed <- plm(mv~crim+zn+indus+chas+nox+rm+age+dis+rad+tax+ptratio+blacks+lstat, data = Hedonic, model = "random", index = "townid") and states it reproduces Baltagi and Chang (1994, table 2) and Baltagi (2005, pp. 172-4; 2013, tables 9.1-9.3): tracts as the observations of an unbalanced panel of towns.

formula: log(oclc) ~ log(libprice / citestot) + I(log(libprice / citestot)^2) + I(log(libprice / citestot)^3) + log(2000 - date1) + log(2000 - date1):log(libprice / citestot) + log(charpp * pages / 1e6) + (1 | pub)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: economics journals in 2000 (Bergstrom) with publisher, library price, pages, characters per page, citations, founding year and library subscriptions (oclc), referenced to Stock and Watson (2003, ch. 6). The book's nonlinear-regression chapter regresses log subscriptions on log price per citation, its square and cube, log age, its interaction with log price per citation and log characters (recalled, not read), by OLS on journals as independent; the interaction of derived terms stays in the formula only. pub repeats across journals, rendered as (1 | pub) by the repeating-cluster ruling at low. oclc is a count the book models in logs, so family gaussian. title is the journal name; society and field are unused.

formula: Ketchup.choice ~ brand intercept + price.<brand> (conditional logit over heinz, hunts, delmonte and stb, one price coefficient) + household-varying brand intercepts and price slope over Ketchup.hid (random-coefficients logit)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: ketchup purchases of households with each brand's price; the loaded columns are named Ketchup.hid, Ketchup.id and Ketchup.choice, and Ketchup.id is the purchase index within the household; the page gives no model. Its source, Kim, Blattberg and Rossi (1995, JBES 13, 291-303), fits by its abstract (IDEAS/RePEc) a random coefficient logit whose brand-level intercepts and price slopes vary across households, on household panel data of two product categories, and tests the parametric heterogeneity distribution against semiparametric density estimates. Rendered as a categorical response with household random effects over Ketchup.hid; the price slope on alternative-specific prices has no lme4 form, so random_slopes stays blank. family blank: categorical responses are outside the contract's family rule.

formula: lnhr ~ lnwg + (1 | id)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: men 1979-1988 (Ziliak 1997), log annual hours, log hourly wage, children, age and bad health, referenced to Cameron and Trivedi (2005, pp. 708-15, 754-6). The book's program for section 21.3 (mma21p1panfeandre.do, cameron.econ.ucdavis.edu/mmabook) fits xtreg lnhr lnwg, re i(id) and xtreg lnhr lnwg, mle i(id) beside pooled OLS, between, within and first differences; its extra regressors (year dummies, kids, ageh, agesq, disab) are commented out. kids, age and disab serve the GMM example of pp. 754-6; year is the time index.

formula: wage ~ school + exper + I(exper^2) + union + maried + ethn + I(industry == "Public_Administration") + (1 | nr)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: young men of the NLS Youth Sample 1980-1987 (Vella and Verbeek 1998), wage the log hourly wage, referenced to Verbeek (2004, ch. 10). Verbeek's panel chapter illustrates wage equations with between, fixed-effects, OLS and random-effects estimates of log wage on schooling, experience and its square, union membership, married, black, Hispanic and public sector (recalled from the cited book, not read). ethn codes black and Hispanic against other; the public sector dummy is written as industry == "Public_Administration", an assumption, and stays in the formula only. health, occupation and residence are unused; year is the time index.

formula: expend ~ revenue + grants + (1 | id)
notes: RULE GAP: Read the Ecdat page: Swedish municipalities 1979-1987 (Dahlberg and Johansson 2000), expenditure, tax and fee revenue and central government grants, referenced to Greene (2003, Table F18.1). The cited paper estimates a dynamic panel vector autoregression of the three series by GMM, and Greene uses the table for dynamic panel GMM (recalled, not read); no mixed model. Rendered as the expenditure equation without its lags, which are no columns, a dynamic panel rendered static; the panel unit id is a random intercept by the panel ruling. The revenue and grants equations are not filed as rows. year is the time index.

formula: log(earnings / hours) ~ educatn + (1 | intnum)
notes: Read the Ecdat page: PSID individuals in 1993 with the 1968 interview number and person number, age, highest grade completed, labor income, annual hours, births and marital status, referenced to Cameron and Trivedi (2005, pp. 295-300). The book's program mma09p1np.do (cameron.econ.ucdavis.edu/mmabook) reads this file as females aged 30 to 50, codes educatn 0, 98 and 99 missing, drops zero earnings, top-codes earnings at 100000, keeps age == 36 and fits lowess and kernel regressions of ln(earnings/hours) on educatn; no parametric model. intnum identifies the 1968 family, which several women share, rendered as (1 | intnum) by the repeating-cluster ruling at low; most families hold one woman. The subset stays in these notes; persnum is the person number within the family; kids and married are unused.
